The Fourier Slice Theorem (FST), also known as the Central Slice Theorem, establishes that the 1D Fourier transform of a projection of a function at angle $\theta$ is equal to a radial slice through the 2D Fourier transform of the original function along the same angle [S1, S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the Fourier Slice Theorem establishes that the 1D Fourier transform of a projection at angle θ is equal to a radial slice through the 2D Fourier transform of the original function along the same angle θ. Source [S1] explicitly states in French: 'Il stipule en effet que... les valeurs des pixels situés sur une ligne inclinée d’un angle θ... sont identiques à celles de la transformée de Fourier de la projection acquise précisément sous cet angle θ' and provides the equation $P̂_{~t} (ν) = f̂(ν cos θ , ν sin θ)$. Source [S2] similarly states: 'Ce théorème définit donc que la transformée F1D de la projection Rθ est égale à la ligne centrée d’angle θ dans l’espace de Fourier F2D du domaine original' and provides the equation $F_θ (ν) = F^{2D}(ψ, ν)|_{ψ=θ}$. Both sources confirm every fact in the claim.
